sections.overview: The meerkat is a small mongoose native to the dry open regions of southern Africa.
sections.identification: It has a slender body, pale coat with darker bands across the back, and often stands upright while watching.
sections.habitat: It uses arid open country and lives in underground burrow systems with multiple entrances.
sections.diet: Its diet is mainly insects, but it also takes other small animals, including scorpions and lizards.
sections.behavior: Groups forage cooperatively, with sentinels giving alarm calls when predators approach.
sections.reproduction: Groups are usually centered on a dominant breeding pair, although other females may also breed.
sections.ecology: Its burrows provide refuge and its cooperative vigilance helps reduce the risk of predation while group members forage.
sections.conservation: It is listed as Least Concern in the global IUCN assessment; local populations may decline during droughts.
